title: Measure: count the probes of a lookup

checklist.step: The reported count equals the membership tests actually made
The bars show your measured counts at three depths

hints: Count an event where it happens. A count worked out from the length of the list is a prediction, not a measurement.
Find the one line of your loop that asks a table whether it holds the name. That line runs once on a hit as well as on every miss before it.
Start a counter at zero for each call and add one each time you are about to test a table; return it beside the value on a hit, and beside None when the chain runs out.

questions.prompt: In the demo's depth-9 chain the name is bound only in the root and the lookup starts at the deepest frame. How many probes?

choices.why: One probe is the cost of a name bound in the starting frame. Here it is at the far end of the chain.
Eight frames miss, but the frame that holds the name is tested too.
Eight misses and then the hit at the root: every frame on the chain is tested once.

questions.prompt: Why can a lookup on a chain of depth d never make more than d probes?

choices.text: It tests each frame on the chain at most once
choices.why: Each step moves to a parent, and a finite chain without cycles never returns to a frame.

choices.text: It tests every binding in every frame
choices.why: A probe asks one table about one name; it does not scan the table's other bindings.

choices.text: Python caches every variable it has read
choices.why: This model has no cache, and the bound does not need one.
